1  For Petitioner : Mr.G.Jeremiah  For R1 to R4 : Mrs.R.L.Karthika,
 Government Advocate  ORDER

This writ petition is filed for issuance of a Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus, calling for the records of the third respondent in his proceedings pertaining to the sub division made in respect of T.S.Nos.81 to 99, Ward B, Block 18, Arakkonam Town dated 15.06.2018 and quash the same and direct respondents 3 and 4 to cancel the sub-divisions in their records and issue a fresh Town Survey Extract in respect of the entire extent of 23 cents of land on the basis of the petitioners application dated 16.12.2019.
2.

Brief facts which are necessary for the disposal of the writ petition are as follows :
2.1

An extent of 23 cents comprised in S.No.199/1A had been purchased by petitioner's grandfather Balaji Rao under a registered sale deed bearing Doc.No.228 of 1935 dated 28.01.1935 on the file of SRO, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Arakkonam.
Thereafter, a superstructure was erected on the site.

The petitioner's grandfather died, leaving behind three sons, namely Parsuramma Rao,
Ramamoorthy Rao, Jayarama Rao who had also died leaving behind their respective legal heirs.
Since the date of purchase of the property, the petitioner's family has been in exclusive possession and enjoyment of the entire property.
The said property has also not been partitioned as it was in a dilapidated condition.
The petitioner's family decided to demolish the existing superstructure and construct a new building over the entire extent.
They approached the bank for financial assistance for raising the construction.
The bank officials directed the petitioner to approach their panel advocate for obtaining a legal title opinion.
The panel advocate requested the petitioner to bring the original documents, patta and extract from Town survey register etc.
Accordingly, the petitioner made an application to the 4th respondent for an extract from the Town Survey.
However, the petitioner found that the 4th respondent municipality had divided the property into 18 sub-divisions and assigned T.S.Nos.81 to 98 for each sub-division.
Most surprisingly, T.S.No.91 had been assigned as Vellaikulam 5th Street and T.S.No.99 as drainage in the revenue record.

2.2 It is further pertinent to note that the survey extract issued to the petitioner does not comprise the entire 23 cents in respect of which the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis petitioner is the registered owner.
Certain portions along the boundary of the property had been excluded from the survey sketch.
Curiously, the northern boundary of the property has been assigned as T.S.No.99 and earmarked as drainage in the Municipal records.
The survey sketch appears to have been prepared by the 3rd respondent.

P.Gopinath Rao vs The Collector on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31764037/
2 2.3
The petitioner was not given any notice regarding the survey to be conducted and had not applied for subdividing the property, nor had he consented for formation of a road bisecting his property.
Respondents 3 and 4 respondents appear to have arbitrarily appropriated portions of their property without their knowledge or consent for the formation of street and drainage.
The property in question is undivided and enjoyed in common by the grandchildren of the registered owner.
2.4 On coming to know the illegal actions of respondents 3 and 4, the petitioner submitted a representation dated 16.12.2019.
Till date, the petitioner has not received any response, nor have the respondents cancelled the illegal sub division.

The petitioner requested for the cancellation of the sub divisions, amalgamate the property into a single holding in his joint names and assign a single Town Survey Number to the entire extent of 23 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis cents.
2.5 The action of respondents 3 and 4 are illegal, arbitrary and without any legal basis.
Respondents 3 and 4 exceeded their jurisdiction.
The right to own property is protected under Article 300A of the Constitution of India and as such, the respondents cannot deprive their property without any legal authority or due process of law.
Section 67 of the Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act empowers the Municipality to acquire land.

Under Section 67 of the Act, the municipality would have to acquire land under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Under Section 61 of the District Municipality Act only the public streets vest with the Municipality.
Admittedly, the property is a private patta land that cannot vest with Municipality until and unless acquisition proceedings are completed.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the impugned order of sub-division of lands which belong to the petitioner was subdivided without giving notice and opportunity, which is a violation of principles of natural justice.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
4. Learned counsel further submitted that according to the sketch of the respondents, the land in Survey Number is shown as Vellaikulam 5th Street in T.S.No.91.

It is also mentioned in the above written instructions that the land in T.S.No.91 belongs to the legal heirs of late Balaji Rao, who is the grandfather of the petitioner and there is a canal in T.S.No.99.
6.

Taking into consideration the factual aspects of the matter, this Court issues the following directions:
a) The impugned order passed by the third respondent sub-dividing the lands made in respect of T.S.Nos.81 to 99, Ward B, Block 18, Arakkonam Town, which belongs to the petitioner herein who is the legal heir of the original owner Balaji Rao is set aside and the land is restored to the original position in respect of 23 cents.
b) This Court remits the matter back to the third respondent for a fresh consideration.
c) The third respondent is directed to conduct a detailed enquiry after giving due notice to both parties, opportunity of personal hearing to the petitioner as well as rival claimants/interested parties if any, to take into consideration the documents filed by the parties and pass appropriate orders on merits, in accordance with law t h e r e b y f o l l o w i n g t h e a b o v e p r i n c i p l e s o f n a t u r a l j u s t i c e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
d) The petitioner is directed to cooperate with the enquiry proceedings conducted by the third respondent.
In the result, the writ petition stands disposed of with the above observation and directions.
